# 2009 NFC Wild Card playoff game (Green Bay–Arizona)

The **2009 NFC Wild Card playoff game** was an American football game played on January 10, 2010, at University of Phoenix Stadium in Glendale, Arizona, between the **Green Bay Packers** and the **Arizona Cardinals**. The Cardinals defeated the Packers in overtime by a score of **51–45**, in what remains the **highest-scoring postseason game in NFL history** with a combined 96 points. 

## Game background

The game featured a matchup between two teams that had met just one week earlier in the regular season, with the Packers winning 33–7 at the same venue. The Cardinals entered the playoffs as the **NFC West champions** with an 11–6 record, while the Packers were the NFC Wild Card team with the same record. 

This game marked several significant milestones:

* It was **Kurt Warner's final NFL playoff game** before his retirement in January 2010 

* It was **Aaron Rodgers' first career playoff start** at quarterback for the Packers 

* The Cardinals were the defending NFC champions, having lost to the Pittsburgh Steelers in Super Bowl XLIII the previous season

## Game summary

### First quarter

The Cardinals dominated the early stages of the game, scoring on their first three possessions. Tim Hightower scored on a 1-yard run just 3:56 into the game, followed by Early Doucet's 15-yard touchdown reception from Kurt Warner. Neil Rackers added a 23-yard field goal to give the Cardinals a commanding **17–0 lead** after the first quarter.

The Packers' offense struggled initially, with Rodgers throwing an interception on the game's first play, which was deflected by Karlos Dansby to Dominique Rodgers-Cromartie. On the Packers' second possession, Donald Driver was stripped by Dansby after a short reception, with Alan Branch recovering for the Cardinals.

### Second quarter

The Packers finally got on the scoreboard with Rodgers scoring on a 1-yard quarterback sneak, capping a 7-play, 68-yard drive. However, the Cardinals quickly responded with Warner connecting with Doucet again for a 15-yard touchdown pass, extending their lead to **24–7**.

The Packers added a 20-yard field goal by Mason Crosby before halftime to make the score **24–10**.

### Third quarter

The Cardinals extended their lead to **31–10** early in the third quarter when Warner found Larry Fitzgerald for a 33-yard touchdown pass. This score came after the Cardinals recovered a Packers fumble on the opening kickoff of the second half.

The Packers then mounted a remarkable comeback, scoring touchdowns on their next three possessions. Rodgers threw touchdown passes to Greg Jennings (6 yards) and Jordy Nelson (11 yards), with an onside kick recovery in between. The Cardinals answered with Warner's fourth touchdown pass of the game, a 11-yard strike to Fitzgerald, making the score **38–24**.

### Fourth quarter

The fourth quarter saw an offensive shootout, with both teams scoring multiple touchdowns. The Packers scored on James Jones' 30-yard reception from Rodgers, and John Kuhn's 1-yard run to tie the game at **38–38**.

The Cardinals regained the lead when Warner connected with Steve Breaston for a 17-yard touchdown pass, making it **45–38**. However, the Packers refused to quit, with Rodgers throwing his fourth touchdown pass of the game, an 11-yarder to Spencer Havner, tying the score at **45–45** with just 1:52 remaining.

The Cardinals had a chance to win the game in regulation when they drove to the Packers' 16-yard line, but Neil Rackers missed a 34-yard field goal attempt wide left with 9 seconds remaining.

### Overtime

The Packers won the overtime coin toss and received the ball, confident they would score and advance. However, on the third play of overtime, Cardinals cornerback Michael Adams (listed at 5'8") sacked Rodgers and forced a fumble. The ball caromed off Rodgers' foot and into the hands of Karlos Dansby, who returned it 17 yards for the game-winning touchdown. 

The play occurred just **78 seconds into overtime**, giving the Cardinals a dramatic **51–45 victory**.

## Key players and performances

### Cardinals

**Kurt Warner** delivered one of the most efficient performances in NFL playoff history, completing **29 of 33 passes** (87.9%) for 379 yards with **five touchdowns and no interceptions**, for a passer rating of 154.1. His five touchdown passes matched his career high, and remarkably, he had **more touchdown passes than incompletions** (five touchdowns vs. four incompletions).

**Larry Fitzgerald** caught six passes for 82 yards and two touchdowns, despite being double-teamed for much of the game. **Early Doucet** had six receptions for 77 yards and two touchdowns, while **Steve Breaston** (starting in place of the injured Anquan Boldin) caught seven passes for 125 yards and one touchdown.

On the ground, **Beanie Wells** rushed for 91 yards on 14 carries (6.5 avg), helping the Cardinals gain 156 rushing yards against the NFL's top-ranked run defense.

**Karlos Dansby** was instrumental on defense, recording two forced fumbles, a fumble recovery, and the game-winning touchdown on the overtime fumble return.

### Packers

**Aaron Rodgers** completed 28 of 42 passes for a **Packers postseason-record 422–423 yards** (sources vary slightly) with four touchdowns and one interception. All but two of his passing yards came after the first quarter, as he led the Packers' comeback from a 21-point deficit. 

**Jermichael Finley** set a Packers playoff record with **159 receiving yards** on six catches, while **Greg Jennings** had eight receptions for 130 yards and one touchdown, including a spectacular one-handed catch.

The Packers' offense was remarkably efficient in the second half, scoring touchdowns on **five consecutive possessions**, with drives covering 80, 57, 80, 67, and 71 yards. No drive took more than four minutes, with five different players scoring touchdowns.

## Game statistics

The game featured remarkable offensive numbers:

| Statistic | Packers | Cardinals |
| ------------------ | -------------- | -------------- |
| Total points | 45 | 51 |
| Total yards | 493 | 531 |
| Passing yards | 404 | 375 |
| Rushing yards | 89 | 156 |
| First downs | 32 | 30 |
| Time of possession | 32:14 | 27:46 |
| Turnovers | 3 | 0 |
| Penalties | 6 for 45 yards | 2 for 15 yards |

The teams combined for:

* **1,024 total yards** (531 for Arizona, 493 for Green Bay)

* **13 touchdowns** (an NFL playoff record)

* **12 combined extra points**

* **96 total points** (the highest combined total in NFL postseason history) 

## Impact and legacy

The game's significance extends beyond the final score:

1. **Historical record**: The 96 combined points broke the previous record of 95 points set in Philadelphia's 58–37 win over Detroit on December 30, 1995. This record still stands as of 2024.

2. **Individual records**:

* Rodgers' 423 passing yards was a Packers postseason record 

* Warner's 87.9% completion percentage remains one of the highest in NFL playoff history

* The game featured the most combined touchdowns (13) in a playoff game

1. **Team records**:

* The Packers scored the **most points by a losing team in NFL playoff history** with 45 points 

* It was the most points scored and allowed by the Packers in their 41-game playoff history

* The Cardinals scored their most points in a playoff game with 51 points 

1. **Player milestones**:

* Warner announced his retirement shortly after the game, ending a Hall of Fame career 

* Rodgers' performance, despite the loss, established him as a premier quarterback in the NFL 

1. **Game-winning play**: The game ended on a defensive touchdown, the first such play to end a playoff game since January 4, 2004, when Al Harris returned an interception 52 yards for a touchdown in Green Bay's 33–27 win over Seattle.

## Subsequent playoff runs

Following this victory, the Cardinals advanced to face the top-seeded New Orleans Saints in the NFC Divisional Round. However, they were soundly defeated 45–14, ending their season. The Saints went on to win Super Bowl XLIV.

The Packers, despite this heartbreaking loss, would return to the playoffs in subsequent seasons, eventually winning Super Bowl XLV following the 2010 season.

## Critical reception

The game was widely praised by players, coaches, and media as one of the greatest playoff games in NFL history. Cardinals coach Ken Whisenhunt called it "probably one of the best games ever played in the playoffs."

Warner himself acknowledged the game's significance, saying at his postgame press conference: "Whew, anybody else tired?" He later described it as "the greatest offensive playoff game in the history of the NFL."

Some media outlets criticized the officiating in the game, with Bleacher Report noting "a far-from-elite performance by the officiating crew." However, specific controversial calls were not detailed in the available sources.

Mike Carey served as the referee for this game.

![Image 3: 100110gamereview215.jpg](https://static.clubs.nfl.com/image/private/t_editorial_landscape_mobile/f_auto/packers/micrjpmu5uh9waeguz1k.jpg)

Arizona CB Michael Adams sacks Green Bay QB Aaron Rodgers, knocking the ball loose. Cardinals LB Karlos Dansby recovered the fumble in midair and raced 17 yards for the game-winning TD in OT.

GLENDALE, Ariz. - It's almost impossible to believe that game could end that way.

In an NFC Wild Card playoff shootout that saw so little defense that more points were scored than in any NFL playoff game in history, it was a defensive play that decided it, in overtime no less.

Arizona cornerback Michael Adams' blitz and sack forced a fumble by Aaron Rodgers that deflected into the arms of Karlos Dansby, and the Cardinals linebacker returned the ball 17 yards for the game-winning score, ending the Packers' season in heartbreaking fashion, 51-45 in front of 61,926 at University of Phoenix Stadium on Sunday.

"The end, I don't know, it was like a dream -- you don't think it's happening, but unfortunately it did," receiver Donald Driver said. "We sat there for a while in shock."

Shocked because the offense had done no wrong since halftime, scoring touchdowns on five straight possessions in the second half to erase a 21-point deficit. The Packers were on such a roll that not one of the five TD drives, which covered 80, 57, 80, 67 and 71 yards, took even four full minutes off the clock, with five different players finding the end zone.

It seemed as though all the Packers needed was one break, and they got it when Arizona's Neil Rackers pulled a potential game-winning 34-yard field goal well left with 9 seconds remaining in regulation. So when Green Bay won the overtime coin toss, no one on the Packers' sideline had any doubt they were going to score and advance to next week's NFC Divisional round.

But it wasn't to be. On the first snap of overtime, receiver Greg Jennings got behind the defense, only to have Rodgers overthrow him on what looked like a sure 80-yard TD. Then a holding penalty wiped out a first down gain, and two snaps later came the decisive turnover, just 78 seconds in all into the extra session.

"I just think that series, the last three plays of the game, I think it's an excellent microcosm of the football game," Head Coach Mike McCarthy said. "You're so close to winning the game on first down and you lose the game on third down."

It appeared the Packers might have lost the game much earlier, and several times in between, due to a couple of early turnovers and a rough day on defense.

Having posted multiple giveaways in only six of 16 games in the regular season, the Packers turned the ball over twice in their first three offensive plays. Rodgers threw an interception on the first snap, making a poor decision to throw across his body after scrambling to the right, and Dansby deflected the ball to Dominique Rodgers-Cromartie.

Then on the second play of the next series, Driver was stripped by Dansby after a short reception, with Alan Branch recovering for the Cardinals.

Arizona took advantage of both miscues, scoring a pair of touchdowns for a 14-0 lead less than six minutes into the game, a jump start that was only the beginning of a dynamite day for quarterback Kurt Warner.

Avoiding any and all pressure with a quick release and his trademark accuracy, Warner played a flawless game that saw him throw more TD passes (five) than incomplete ones (four) in going 29-of-33 for 379 yards and a sterling 154.1 passer rating. Receiver Steve Breaston, starting for an injured Anquan Boldin (ankle), posted seven catches for 125 yards, while Larry Fitzgerald (6-82) and Early Doucet (6-77) caught two TD passes apiece.

Combined with a ground game that posted 156 yards, nearly double the Packers' average as the No. 1 run defense in the league this season (83.3 ypg), the Cardinals were so efficient they faced third down just five times on the day in nine total possessions.

"Today it just seemed like Warner had our number," rookie linebacker Clay Matthews said. "It was tough."

An Arizona TD drive on the opening possession of the second half, capped by Fitzgerald's 33-yard catch-and-run after a collision with Charles Woodson knocked the Packers' top defender down, established the Cardinals' biggest lead of the game at 31-10.

But the Packers rallied time and again behind Rodgers and an equally dangerous receiving corps led by Jermichael Finley and Jennings.

Rodgers threw for a franchise playoff-record 422 yards on 28-of-42 passing, with four TDs and the one interception for a 121.3 rating. Finley set a team record for receiving yards in the playoffs with 159 on six grabs, and Jennings made two spectacular catches, one a one-hander for a TD and another a tip-toe job down the sideline, among his eight receptions for 130 yards.

The rally began in earnest when the Packers got back-to-back touchdowns in the third quarter, with the help of a surprise onside kick in between, to get within 31-24. Then the shootout was in full force.

Arizona answered by going 73 yards in three plays, the biggest a 42-yard run by Beanie Wells (14 carries, 91 yards) to set up a diving 11-yard TD grab by Fitzgerald to restore a 14-point lead.

The Packers responded with an 80-yard march, getting a 30-yard TD pass to James Jones on fourth-and-5. Then the defense got its lone stop of the second half (and first since a second-quarter turnover began the initial comeback from a 17-0 hole), forcing Arizona's sole punt of the game early in the fourth quarter.

The Packers then needed just three plays to tie the game, with fullback John Kuhn's 1-yard dive knotting things at 38 with 11 minutes left.

The Cardinals had yet another answer, as Breaston's TD catch capped an 11-play, 80-yard march, but the Packers had one more score in them, too, as Rodgers' 11-yard TD pass to Spencer Havner re-tied the game at 45 with 1:52 left.

{sportsad300}That set up the drive that ended in Rackers' miss, leading to the overtime. All the while it seemed like one more defensive stop might have finally shifted momentum for good, but the Packers couldn't get it. Ultimately, the Cardinals did, and in dramatic fashion.

"Yeah, we'd been saying that for a while as a defense," linebacker A.J. Hawk said. "We knew if we could get off the field the offense was going to score and get the lead. A lot of times we didn't get that stop and our offense kept coming back for us.

"It was one of those things where we needed a big stop, a turnover, something to change the tide of the game. We didn't get that when we needed to and obviously they did at the end."

It was about as difficult a way to fall in the playoffs as anyone could imagine, particularly after such a heart-stirring, never-say-die comeback on top of a 7-1 run in the second half of the season to get a playoff shot.

"Woulda, coulda, shoulda," Jennings said. "What if? If this, if that. The reality of it is our season is over."

Too soon for sure, in a game so close several players afterward were pondering many of Jennings' same thoughts, unfortunately now with a long offseason to do so.

"This one's going to hurt for a while," Driver said. "We felt like this was our year."

Cardinals Folktales - Money Mike's Redemption

Cardinals Folktales - Money Mike's Redemption
=============================================

Ep. 8 - In the 2009 NFC Wild Card game, the Cardinals and Packers lit up the scoreboard thanks to epic performances from QBs Kurt Warner and Aaron Rodgers. However the game was decided on defense when the smallest player on the field came up with the biggest play of his life. Paul Calvisi tells the story of Money Mike Adams who was able to overcome several miscues to lift the Cardinals to an overtime victory in one of the greatest postseason contests of all time.

[![Image 4: Football player in uniform with a football in his hands over a black background with the words Folktales and When Arizona Met the Cardiac Cards in white letters](https://static.clubs.nfl.com/image/upload/t_editorial_landscape_mobile/f_auto/cardinals/spyzbdde38to8yesl7be.jpg) NOW PLAYING audio ### Cardinals Folktales - When Arizona Met The Cardiac Cards When the Cardinals moved to Arizona in 1988, there was a major buzz around the Valley of the Sun. A high-powered offense led by quarterback Neil Lomax and wide receiver Roy Green gave Phoenix Cardinals fans many exciting moments during their debut season, none more thrilling than an epic second-half comeback against the loaded San Francisco 49ers. Paul Calvisi tells the story of how the Cardinals erased a 23-0 third-quarter deficit to stun the eventual Super Bowl Champs at Sun Devil Stadium. What followed was a major gut punch that would put a premature end to Lomax's career.](https://www.azcardinals.com/podcasts/cardinals-folktales-when-arizona-met-the-cardiac-cards-the-podcast "Cardinals Folktales - When Arizona Met The Cardiac Cards")

[![Image 5: Kurt Warner is celebrating while wearing a jersey with number 13](https://static.clubs.nfl.com/image/private/t_editorial_landscape_mobile/f_auto/cardinals/w0xm5g3dxqshuzrvvh5x.jpg) NOW PLAYING audio ### Cardinals Folktales - Kurt Warner: Renaissance Man Kurt Warner arrived in Arizona in 2005 looking to revive his career in search of the same glory he achieved with the St. Louis Rams. The two-time MVP and Super Bowl winning quarterback had to prove himself all over again. Warner overcame the odds, silenced his doubters, won the starting job and eventually led the Cardinals to their first Super Bowl appearance. Paul Calvisi details the ups and downs of Kurt's career in Arizona, an improbable era that sealed his position in the Pro Football Hall of Fame.](https://www.azcardinals.com/podcasts/cardinals-folktales-kurt-warner-renaissance-man-the-podcast "Cardinals Folktales - Kurt Warner: Renaissance Man")

[![Image 6: Folktales, episode three, Lassiter's Legacy](https://static.clubs.nfl.com/image/upload/t_editorial_landscape_mobile/f_auto/cardinals/egin9kanjnp99h1f1apl.jpg) NOW PLAYING audio ### Cardinals Folktales - Lassiter's Legacy S2, E3 - Kwamie Lassiter the football player may be best remembered for his four-interception game that helped send the 1998 Cardinals to the playoffs for the first time since arriving in Arizona. Kwamie Lassiter the man will be remembered for much more. Paul Calvisi explores Lassiter's path to a successful NFL career, his larger-than-life personality, the special relationship he forged with Pat Tillman, teaming with his wife Ericka to be champions in the community and his tragic passing in 2019. Lassiter's legacy lives on through The Kwamie Lassiter Foundation which focuses on Sickle Cell awareness and educational resources for those who need it most.](https://www.azcardinals.com/podcasts/cardinals-folktales-lassiter-s-legacy-the-podcast "Cardinals Folktales - Lassiter's Legacy")

[![Image 7: Folktales, Episode Two, Miracle in the Desert features images of a football game and a post-game hug](https://static.clubs.nfl.com/image/upload/t_editorial_landscape_mobile/f_auto/cardinals/adspmrxv9fjcp5lylzxo.jpg) NOW PLAYING audio ### Cardinals Folktales - Miracle In The Desert S2, E2 - The final game of the 2003 season against the Vikings was expected to be a formality for the Cardinals. It was anything but that. Paul Calvisi tells the story of an unknown receiver making the biggest play of his life while sending shockwaves through three NFL markets and significantly altering the 2004 NFL Draft. In a matter of seconds, Nathan Poole won the game for the Cardinals, pushed the Packers into the playoffs and broke the hearts of the Vikings and their fans.](https://www.azcardinals.com/podcasts/cardinals-folktales-miracle-in-the-desert-the-podcast "Cardinals Folktales - Miracle In The Desert")

[![Image 8: An original motion picture soundtrack of the film Godzilla](https://static.clubs.nfl.com/image/upload/t_editorial_landscape_mobile/t_lazy/f_auto/cardinals/bml4rjiscxt4tpaskoil.jpg) NOW PLAYING audio ### Cardinals Folktales - The Hyphen Wins A House S2, E1 - Former Cardinals running back and kick returner LaRod Stephens-Howling made several incredible plays during his four seasons in Arizona, but it was a kick return during the 2010 season that had the biggest impact. In the Cardinals' home opener against the Raiders, 'The Hyphen' took the opening kickoff to the house and won a house for a local couple. This is the story of how the stars aligned that September afternoon to allow a kick return to produce big returns for Cardinals fan Dave Johnson and his wife Darci Nimz.](https://www.azcardinals.com/podcasts/cardinals-folktales-the-hyphen-wins-a-house-the-podcast "Cardinals Folktales - The Hyphen Wins A House")

[![Image 9: The graphic image shows an arrangement of blurred images, possibly portraits or abstract forms](https://static.clubs.nfl.com/image/private/t_editorial_landscape_mobile/t_lazy/f_auto/cardinals/tuvpq3ptag7t1gctn7kn.jpg) NOW PLAYING audio ### Cardinals Folktales - Snow Day To Tampa Bay Ep. 11 - When the 2008 Cardinals were dismantled by the Patriots in wintery conditions, many experts gave Arizona a snowball's chance in hell to succeed in the playoffs. After some brutal practices in the rain, the newly-focused Cardinals played well in the season finale before going on an epic run to earn a spot in Super Bowl XLIII. Paul Calvisi details the journey from nightmare roadtrip to the biggest stage in sports.](https://www.azcardinals.com/podcasts/cardinals-folktales-snow-day-to-tampa-bay-the-podcast "Cardinals Folktales - Snow Day To Tampa Bay")

[![Image 10: Black and white still of The Who, with John Entwistle in the center](https://static.clubs.nfl.com/image/private/t_editorial_landscape_mobile/t_lazy/f_auto/cardinals/t4jiexw2drhpubvkf4ge.jpg) NOW PLAYING audio ### Cardinals Folktales - Nine More Ep. 10 - In 2013, former Cardinals safety Rashad Johnson lost more than a football game in New Orleans. He literally lost a part of himself. Paul Calvisi tells the tale of a bloody glove, severed fingertip and viral tweet that made for one of the most bizarre stories in NFL history.](https://www.azcardinals.com/podcasts/cardinals-folktales-nine-more-the-podcast "Cardinals Folktales - Nine More")

[![Image 11: Three blurry posters, each with a different movie title and image](https://static.clubs.nfl.com/image/private/t_editorial_landscape_mobile/t_lazy/f_auto/cardinals/ossmffisw9tnxaq8ntbq.jpg) NOW PLAYING audio ### Cardinals Folktales - Thanks, Coach Ep. 9 - When it comes to epic postgame rants, you can go ahead and crown Dennis Green's "The Bears are who we thought they were" tirade from 2006. Paul Calvisi explores several different layers of Denny's monumental meltdown that followed a truly remarkable Monday Night Football game against the Bears. How did the Cardinals blow a 20-point halftime lead? Did Green actually call his shot before meeting the media? And what exactly did he mean? Countdown to meltdown in 3-2-1.](https://www.azcardinals.com/podcasts/cardinals-folktales-thanks-coach-the-podcast-x9031 "Cardinals Folktales - Thanks, Coach")

**Kurtis Eugene "Kurt" Warner** (born June 22, 1971, in [Burlington](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burlington,_Iowa "Burlington, Iowa"), [Iowa](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iowa "Iowa"))[[1]](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurt_Warner#cite_note-1) is a retired [American](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States")[football](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_football "American football") player. He was the [quarterback](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quarterback "Quarterback") for the [Arizona Cardinals](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arizona_Cardinals "Arizona Cardinals"). After playing in [college](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/College "College") at [Northern Iowa](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Northern_Iowa "University of Northern Iowa"), he was signed by the [Green Bay Packers](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Bay_Packers "Green Bay Packers") as an [undrafted free agent](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Undrafted_sportsperson "Undrafted sportsperson").[[2]](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurt_Warner#cite_note-2) He was not able to play there, so he went to the [Arena Football League](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arena_Football_League "Arena Football League"), and then later the [NFL Europa](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFL_Europa "NFL Europa").[[3]](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurt_Warner#cite_note-3)

In 1998, Warner was signed by the [St. Louis Rams](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Louis_Rams "St. Louis Rams"). After the Rams' main quarterback [Trent Green](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trent_Green "Trent Green") went out with an [injury](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Injury "Injury"), Warner became the main quarterback. He later went on to [win](https://simple.wiktionary.org/wiki/win "wikt:win")[NFL MVP awards](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_League_Most_Valuable_Player_Award "National Football League Most Valuable Player Award") in 1999 and 2001, as well as the [Super Bowl MVP award](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_Most_Valuable_Player_Award "Super Bowl Most Valuable Player Award") in 2000.[[4]](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurt_Warner#cite_note-4)

In 1990, Kurt [graduated](https://simple.wiktionary.org/wiki/graduate "wikt:graduate") from [Regis High School](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regis_High_School_(Cedar_Rapids) "Regis High School (Cedar Rapids)") in [Cedar Rapids](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cedar_Rapids,_Iowa "Cedar Rapids, Iowa"), Iowa.[[5]](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurt_Warner#cite_note-5) While there, he played quarterback of the school's Class 3A [football](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Football "Football")[team](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team "Team"). He announced his retirement from football on January 29, 2010.[[6]](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurt_Warner#cite_note-6)

[![Image 2: Group of medical professionals interacting with a patient](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/69/Kurt_Warner_and_Amani_Toomer.jpg/250px-Kurt_Warner_and_Amani_Toomer.jpg)](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Kurt_Warner_and_Amani_Toomer.jpg)

Warner (center) and his wife Brenda (left), with former teammate [Amani Toomer](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amani_Toomer "Amani Toomer") (right) visited a sick [Indonesian](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indonesia "Indonesia")[boy](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boy "Boy").

After Warner graduated from [high school](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/High_school "High school"), he went to the University of Northern Iowa (UNI). At UNI, Warner was third on the Panthers' [depth chart](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Depth_chart "Depth chart") until his [senior year](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twelfth_grade "Twelfth grade"). In his final year there, he was able to start and was named the [Gateway Conference](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri_Valley_Football_Conference "Missouri Valley Football Conference")'s Offensive Player of the Year.[[7]](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurt_Warner#cite_note-7)

While at college, he met future wife, the former Brenda Carney Meoni. They got married on October 11, 1997. Before this, Brenda had served in the [Marines](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Marine_Corps "United States Marine Corps"). She was divorced with two children when they met each other. Warner [adopted](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adoption "Adoption") Brenda's two children, son Zachary and daughter Jesse, after their marriage.[[8]](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurt_Warner#cite_note-8) Zachary is [blind](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindness "Blindness") from the [head](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Head "Head") injuries he got when he was [accidentally](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Accident "Accident") dropped by his birth-father as a [baby](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baby "Baby").[[9]](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurt_Warner#cite_note-9) Warner agreed to help Brenda raise the children. The Warners now also have five children of their own: sons Elijah and Kade, daughter Jada, and twin girls Sierra Rose and Sienna Rae.[[10]](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurt_Warner#cite_note-10)

After being let go from the Green Bay Packers [training camp](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_League_Training_Camp "National Football League Training Camp") in 1994, he got a job working the [night shift](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shift_work "Shift work") at a local [Fareway](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fareway "Fareway") grocery store. He was also assistant-coaching at Northern Iowa. Warner still wanted to play in the NFL, but with that not seeming it was going to happen, and the long hours at the Fareway for [minimum wage](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minimum_wage "Minimum wage") creating [financial](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finance "Finance") trouble for him,[[11]](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurt_Warner#cite_note-11) Warner began playing in the Arena Football League. In 1996 and almost a year before Kurt and Brenda's marriage, Brenda's parents, Larry and Jenny Carney, were killed when their [Arkansas](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arkansas "Arkansas") home was destroyed by a [tornado](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tornado "Tornado").[[12]](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurt_Warner#cite_note-12)

Both Kurt and his wife are active [born again Christians](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Born_again_Christianity "Born again Christianity").[_[source?](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citing\_sources "Wikipedia:Citing sources")_]

On October 24, 2006, Warner was in a [political](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Politics "Politics")[advertisement](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Advertisement "Advertisement") against a [proposed](https://simple.wiktionary.org/wiki/propose "wikt:propose")[law](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Law "Law") in [Missouri](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri "Missouri"). That new law would allow [embryonic stem cell research](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embryonic_stem_cell "Embryonic stem cell") to be done in Missouri.[[13]](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurt_Warner#cite_note-13) Warner was in the advertisement with [James Caviezel](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Caviezel "Jim Caviezel"), [Patricia Heaton](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patricia_Heaton "Patricia Heaton"), [Jeff Suppan](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeff_Suppan "Jeff Suppan"), and [Mike Sweeney](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Sweeney "Mike Sweeney").[[14]](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurt_Warner#cite_note-14) The advertisement, which was played during Game 4 of the 2006 [World Series](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Series "World Series"), falsely alleged that [Amendment](https://simple.wiktionary.org/wiki/amendment "wikt:amendment") 2 would allow [human cloning](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_cloning "Human cloning").[[15]](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurt_Warner#cite_note-15) The advertisement came after a pro-embryonic research advertisement that had [Michael J. Fox](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_J._Fox "Michael J. Fox"), who has [Parkinson's disease](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parkinson's_disease "Parkinson's disease"), in it.

Warner went to the [Green Bay Packers](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Bay_Packers "Green Bay Packers") training camp in 1994, but was [released](https://simple.wiktionary.org/wiki/release "wikt:release") before the regular season began. He returned to Northern Iowa and worked as a graduate assistant coach with the football team, but he still wanted to get a [tryout](https://simple.wiktionary.org/wiki/tryout "wikt:tryout") with an NFL team. When no NFL team would give him a tryout, Warner began playing for the [Arena Football League](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arena_Football_League "Arena Football League"). In 1995, he signed with the [Iowa Barnstormers](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Dragons "New York Dragons"). Warner was named to the AFL's All-Arena first team in both 1996 and 1997. He [led](https://simple.wiktionary.org/wiki/leader "wikt:leader") the Barnstormers to the [Arena Bowl](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arena_Bowl "Arena Bowl") in both 1996 and 1997. Some people [consider](https://simple.wiktionary.org/wiki/consider "wikt:consider") Warner one of the greatest Arena Football player of all-time.[[16]](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurt_Warner#cite_note-16)

In 1997, Warner was [offered](https://simple.wiktionary.org/wiki/offer "wikt:offer") an NFL tryout by the [Chicago Bears](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Bears "Chicago Bears"), but he could not [attend](https://simple.wiktionary.org/wiki/attend "wikt:attend") the tryout. In 1998, he was signed by the [St. Louis Rams](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Louis_Rams "St. Louis Rams"), but he only played for [NFL Europe's](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFL_Europa "NFL Europa")[Amsterdam Admirals](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amsterdam_Admirals "Amsterdam Admirals").[[17]](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurt_Warner#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurt_Warner#cite_note-18)

Warner was the backup quarterback for the [St. Louis Rams](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Louis_Rams "St. Louis Rams") during the 1998 regular season and the 1999 [preseason](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Preseason "Preseason"). When their main quarterback [Trent Green](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trent_Green "Trent Green") was injured in a preseason game, Warner became the starter. He had one of the best seasons by a quarterback in NFL [history](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/History "History") by throwing for 4,353 [yards](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yard "Yard") with 41 [touchdown](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Touchdown "Touchdown")[passes](https://simple.wiktionary.org/wiki/pass "wikt:pass") and a completion rate of 65.1[%](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Percent "Percent"). The Rams' very good [offense](https://simple.wiktionary.org/wiki/offense "wikt:offense") was [nicknamed](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nickname "Nickname") "[The Greatest Show on Turf](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Greatest_Show_on_Turf "The Greatest Show on Turf")." In the first three games that he was the main quarterback who plays, he threw three touchdown passes in each game. He is the only NFL quarterback in history to do that, and only the second, behind [Dan Marino](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Marino "Dan Marino"), to do it in his first two NFL starts.

Because not many people knew who Warner was, _[Sports Illustrated](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sports\_Illustrated "Sports Illustrated")_ put him on their October 18, 1999 cover with the caption "Who IS this guy?"[[19]](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurt_Warner#cite_note-19) He was named the 1999 NFL MVP at the end of the season. In the [NFL playoffs](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_League_playoffs "National Football League playoffs"), he led the Rams to a [Super Bowl XXXIV](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XXXIV "Super Bowl XXXIV") win against the [Tennessee Titans](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennessee_Titans "Tennessee Titans").[[20]](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurt_Warner#cite_note-20) He threw for two touchdowns and a Super Bowl record 414 passing yards. He also set a Super Bowl record by [throwing](https://simple.wiktionary.org/wiki/throw "wikt:throw") 45 passes without an [interception](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interception_(football) "Interception (football)").[[21]](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurt_Warner#cite_note-21)

Right after the Rams' Super Bowl win, an [interviewer](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interview "Interview") asked Warner, "Kurt, first things first--tell me about the [final](https://simple.wiktionary.org/wiki/final "wikt:final") touchdown pass to Isaac." He [responded](https://simple.wiktionary.org/wiki/respond "wikt:respond"), "Well, first things first, I've got to thank my [Lord](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lord "Lord") and [Savior](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Savior "Savior") up above--thank You, [Jesus](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesus "Jesus")!" [[22]](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurt_Warner#cite_note-eads-22) He was awarded the [Super Bowl MVP](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_MVP "Super Bowl MVP"). That made him one of only six players to win both the league MVP and Super Bowl MVP awards in the same year. The others are [Bart Starr](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bart_Starr "Bart Starr") in 1966, [Terry Bradshaw](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terry_Bradshaw "Terry Bradshaw") in 1978, [Joe Montana](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Montana "Joe Montana") in 1989, [Emmitt Smith](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emmitt_Smith "Emmitt Smith") in 1993, and [Steve Young](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Young_(football_player) "Steve Young (football player)") in 1994.

Warner also played well in the 2000 season. Warner and Trent Green both played quarterback that season, and they both played well. But the Rams lost in the [wild card round](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wild_card_(sports) "Wild card (sports)") of the playoffs to the [New Orleans Saints](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Orleans_Saints "New Orleans Saints"),[[23]](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurt_Warner#cite_note-23) mostly because their [defense](https://simple.wiktionary.org/wiki/defense "wikt:defense") was not very good, even though Warner and the rest of their offense was still very good. Nine of the Rams' eleven defensive starters were cut in the [offseason](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Offseason "Offseason"), and Green was traded to the [Kansas City Chiefs](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_City_Chiefs "Kansas City Chiefs").[[24]](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurt_Warner#cite_note-24)

Warner played very well in the 2001 season. He had a league-high 36 touchdown passes and 4,830 passing yards with a career-high completion rate of 68.7% of his passes. He led the Rams to an NFL-best 14–2 record and they went to the [Super Bowl XXXVI](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XXXVI "Super Bowl XXXVI"), but they lost to the [New England Patriots](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_England_Patriots "New England Patriots").[[25]](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurt_Warner#cite_note-25) He was named the NFL MVP for the second time at the end of the season.[[26]](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurt_Warner#cite_note-26)

Warner began the season 0–3 as a starter, throwing seven interceptions with only one touchdown. In their fourth game against the [Dallas Cowboys](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas_Cowboys "Dallas Cowboys"), he broke a [finger](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finger "Finger") on his throwing hand.[[27]](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurt_Warner#cite_note-27) Even thought he tried to come back later in the season, his injury caused him to be able to play two more games, and he lost them both. In [contrast](https://simple.wiktionary.org/wiki/contrast "wikt:contrast") to his 103.4 career [passer rating](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Passer_rating "Passer rating") before that season, he had only 67.4 rating in 2002. He was replaced as the Rams' main quarterback after he [fumbled](https://simple.wiktionary.org/wiki/fumble "wikt:fumble") six times in the opener of the 2003 season against the [New York Giants](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Giants "New York Giants"). His replacement as the Rams quarterback, [Marc Bulger](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marc_Bulger "Marc Bulger"), has been named to two [Pro Bowls](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pro_Bowl "Pro Bowl").[[28]](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurt_Warner#cite_note-28)

The Rams released Warner on June 1, 2004. Just two days later, he signed a two-year [deal](https://simple.wiktionary.org/wiki/deal "wikt:deal") with the New York Giants. He began the 2004 season as the main quarterback. He won five of his first seven games, but after not playing well in a two-game losing streak, [rookie](https://simple.wiktionary.org/wiki/rookie "wikt:rookie") quarterback [Eli Manning](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eli_Manning "Eli Manning") was made the main quarterback. Giants [coach](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coach_(sport) "Coach (sport)")[Tom Coughlin](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Coughlin "Tom Coughlin") later said that he never should have made Warner play, and should have played Manning from the beginning to give Manning the [experience](https://simple.wiktionary.org/wiki/experience "wikt:experience") he needs to build his [confidence](https://simple.wiktionary.org/wiki/confidence "wikt:confidence"). The Giants had a 5–4 win-loss record at the time that Manning began playing, and they finished at 6–10 overall (going only 1–6 under Manning).[[29]](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurt_Warner#cite_note-29)

In early 2005, Warner signed a one-year, [$](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/US_dollar "US dollar")4-million [contract](https://simple.wiktionary.org/wiki/contract "wikt:contract") with the [Arizona Cardinals](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arizona_Cardinals "Arizona Cardinals"). He was soon named the main quarterback by coach [Dennis Green](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dennis_Green "Dennis Green"). He played bad in three games before injuring his [groin](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Groin "Groin"). He was then replaced by former starter [Josh McCown](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josh_McCown "Josh McCown"). McCown played well enough in two games during Warner's injury to get coach Green named McCown the starter for the rest of the season.

As Warner was the backup quarterback, many people thought that he was never to be the main quarterback again. But because McCown played bad in two straight games, coach Green made Warner the main quarterback. He played well in the next three weeks, but his season ended in Week 15 when he partly tore his [MCL](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medial_collateral_ligament "Medial collateral ligament").[[30]](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurt_Warner#cite_note-30)

Warner signed a new three-year deal with the Cardinals on February 14, 2006.[[31]](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurt_Warner#cite_note-31) The deal had a base [salary](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salary "Salary") of $18 million, but if he played well, he could get as much as $22 million in the three years.[[32]](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurt_Warner#cite_note-32)

In Week 3 of the 2006 season, Warner passed the 20,000-yards passing milestone in his 76th game.[[33]](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurt_Warner#cite_note-33) That was one game more than [record](https://simple.wiktionary.org/wiki/record "wikt:record") holder Dan Marino, but Warner did it in his 9th year while Marino did it in his 5th.[[34]](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurt_Warner#cite_note-34) After [Matt Leinart](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matt_Leinart "Matt Leinart") played poorly in the three games of Weeks 2-4, Warner [replaced](https://simple.wiktionary.org/wiki/replace "wikt:replace") the rookie Leinart in the fourth quarter of Week 4.[[35]](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurt_Warner#cite_note-35)[[36]](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurt_Warner#cite_note-36) In Week 16, Leinart had a [shoulder](https://simple.wiktionary.org/wiki/shoulder "wikt:shoulder") injury against the [San Francisco 49ers](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco_49ers "San Francisco 49ers"), so Warner was able to play for the first time since Week 4. He did well that game, and the Cardinals won the game.[[37]](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurt_Warner#cite_note-37)

In the third game of the 2007 season against the [Baltimore Ravens](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baltimore_Ravens "Baltimore Ravens"),[[38]](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurt_Warner#cite_note-38) Warner came off the bench because Leinart was again not playing well. He led a [comeback](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comeback "Comeback"), [completing](https://simple.wiktionary.org/wiki/complete "wikt:complete") 15 passes out of 20 attempts for 258 yards and 2 touchdowns. This brought them to a [tie](https://simple.wiktionary.org/wiki/tie "wikt:tie") game (23–23), but after the Ravens made a last second field goal, Arizona lost the game 26–23.[[39]](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurt_Warner#cite_note-39) On September 30, 2007, during the Week 4 game against the [Pittsburgh Steelers](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pittsburgh_Steelers "Pittsburgh Steelers"), he went in for Leinart because he was not playing well again. Leinart was later placed on [Injured reserve](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Injured_reserve_list "Injured reserve list"), so Warner was named the starter for the rest of the 2007 season.[[40]](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurt_Warner#cite_note-40)

Warner got 27 passing touchdowns in the 2007 season, just one short of the Cardinals [franchise](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franchise "Franchise") record. Because he played well, he was given a $1 million [bonus](https://simple.wiktionary.org/wiki/bonus "wikt:bonus") for the year. His 3,417 passing yards, 27 touchdown passes, and 89.8 passer rating were all his best since the 2001 season.[[41]](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurt_Warner#cite_note-41)

Matt Leinart was named the Cardinals starter going in to the off-season for 2008, but [Ken Whisenhunt](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Whisenhunt "Ken Whisenhunt") said that it may happen that Warner become the Cardinals' starter before the season begins. Warner was named the starter on August 30, 2008. That season, Warner had a very good season, and on December 16, 2008, was named the starting quarterback for the NFC team in the 2009 [Pro Bowl](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pro_Bowl "Pro Bowl").[[42]](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurt_Warner#cite_note-42) Warner and the Cardinals won all three of their playoff games, but lost in the [Super Bowl](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl "Super Bowl") to the [Pittsburgh Steelers](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pittsburgh_Steelers "Pittsburgh Steelers"). That makes Warner's Super Bowl record 1–2. [James Dobson](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Dobson "James Dobson"), starter of [Focus on the Family](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Focus_on_the_Family "Focus on the Family"), has been supportive of Warner,[[43]](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurt_Warner#cite_note-43) and even replayed a radio clip of Warner and his wife on January 30, 2009.[[44]](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurt_Warner#cite_note-44)

13.title: マイク・キャリー
13.content:
出典: フリー百科事典『ウィキペディア（Wikipedia）』

| マイク・キャリー Mike Carey |
| --- |
| [![Image 1: Smiling bald Black man wearing a black NFL Nike jacket](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/7/70/Referee_Mike_Carey.jpg)](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E3%83%95%E3%82%A1%E3%82%A4%E3%83%AB:Referee_Mike_Carey.jpg) |
| 生誕 | Michael Carey [1949年](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/1949%E5%B9%B4 "1949年")[8月17日](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/8%E6%9C%8817%E6%97%A5 "8月17日")（76歳） [カリフォルニア州](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E3%82%AB%E3%83%AA%E3%83%95%E3%82%A9%E3%83%AB%E3%83%8B%E3%82%A2%E5%B7%9E "カリフォルニア州") [サンディエゴ](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E3%82%B5%E3%83%B3%E3%83%87%E3%82%A3%E3%82%A8%E3%82%B4 "サンディエゴ") |
| 国籍 | [![Image 2: アメリカ合衆国の旗](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a4/Flag_of_the_United_States.svg/40px-Flag_of_the_United_States.svg.png)](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E3%83%95%E3%82%A1%E3%82%A4%E3%83%AB:Flag_of_the_United_States.svg "アメリカ合衆国の旗")[アメリカ合衆国](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E3%82%A2%E3%83%A1%E3%83%AA%E3%82%AB%E5%90%88%E8%A1%86%E5%9B%BD "アメリカ合衆国") |
| 教育 | [サンタクララ大学](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E3%82%B5%E3%83%B3%E3%82%BF%E3%82%AF%E3%83%A9%E3%83%A9%E5%A4%A7%E5%AD%A6 "サンタクララ大学")(1971) |
| 職業 | [NFL](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFL "NFL")審判員(1990–2013) セイラス社共同設立者 |
| 配偶者 | Wendy Carey |
| 子供 | 2 |
| [テンプレートを表示](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/Template:Infobox_%E4%BA%BA%E7%89%A9 "Template:Infobox 人物") |

**マイク・キャリー** (**Michael Carey**、[1949年](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/1949%E5%B9%B4 "1949年")[8月17日](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/8%E6%9C%8817%E6%97%A5 "8月17日") - ) は、[アメリカ合衆国](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E3%82%A2%E3%83%A1%E3%83%AA%E3%82%AB%E5%90%88%E8%A1%86%E5%9B%BD "アメリカ合衆国")の[実業家](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E5%BC%81%E8%AD%B7%E5%A3%AB "弁護士")、元[アメリカンフットボール](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E3%82%A2%E3%83%A1%E3%83%AA%E3%82%AB%E3%83%B3%E3%83%95%E3%83%83%E3%83%88%E3%83%9C%E3%83%BC%E3%83%AB "アメリカンフットボール")[審判員](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E5%AF%A9%E5%88%A4%E5%93%A1 "審判員")である。[ナショナルフットボールリーグ](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFL "NFL")（NFL）で長く審判を務めた。[アフリカ系アメリカ人](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E3%82%A2%E3%83%95%E3%83%AA%E3%82%AB%E7%B3%BB%E3%82%A2%E3%83%A1%E3%83%AA%E3%82%AB%E4%BA%BA "アフリカ系アメリカ人")として初めて[スーパーボウル](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E3%82%B9%E3%83%BC%E3%83%91%E3%83%BC%E3%83%9C%E3%82%A6%E3%83%AB "スーパーボウル")でレフェリー（主審）を担当した[[1]](https://ja.wikipedia.org/?curid=4601631#cite_note-:0-1)[[2]](https://ja.wikipedia.org/?curid=4601631#cite_note-:1-2)ほか、多くのプレーオフのレフェリーを務めた。

試合前の徹底した準備、プロフェッショナルな態度、フェアプレーでNFLの審判員として尊敬を集めていた[[3]](https://ja.wikipedia.org/?curid=4601631#cite_note-:2-3)[[4]](https://ja.wikipedia.org/?curid=4601631#cite_note-4)。2008年に[ESPN](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/ESPN "ESPN")が行った投票では、NFLの[ヘッドコーチ](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E3%83%98%E3%83%83%E3%83%89%E3%82%B3%E3%83%BC%E3%83%81 "ヘッドコーチ")が選ぶ「最高の審判」投票で、キャリーは[エド・ホキュリ](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E3%82%A8%E3%83%89%E3%83%BB%E3%83%9B%E3%82%AD%E3%83%A5%E3%83%AA "エド・ホキュリ")と並んで最多得票を獲得した[[5]](https://ja.wikipedia.org/?curid=4601631#cite_note-5)。また、退場宣告を多く出していることでも知られている[[6]](https://ja.wikipedia.org/?curid=4601631#cite_note-:3-6)。

24年間のNFLでのキャリアで、ワイルドカード・プレーオフ10回、ディビジョナル・プレーオフ5回、カンファレンス・チャンピオンシップ2回、第42回スーパーボウルの計18回のポストシーズンの試合でレフェリーを務めた[[2]](https://ja.wikipedia.org/?curid=4601631#cite_note-:1-2)。

1971年、[サンタクララ大学](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E3%82%B5%E3%83%B3%E3%82%BF%E3%82%AF%E3%83%A9%E3%83%A9%E5%A4%A7%E5%AD%A6 "サンタクララ大学")で[生物学](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E7%94%9F%E7%89%A9%E5%AD%A6 "生物学")の学士号を取得[[3]](https://ja.wikipedia.org/?curid=4601631#cite_note-:2-3)。在学中の4年間はフットボールチームに在籍し[ランニングバック](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E3%83%A9%E3%83%B3%E3%83%8B%E3%83%B3%E3%82%B0%E3%83%90%E3%83%83%E3%82%AF "ランニングバック")として活躍したが、足首の怪我により選手を引退した。この怪我はその後も尾を引いており、試合の審判をする日以外は走ることができなかった[[6]](https://ja.wikipedia.org/?curid=4601631#cite_note-:3-6)。

1972年、友人の勧めでカリフォルニア州サンディエゴ地域のポップワーナーフットボールの試合で審判を始めた[[6]](https://ja.wikipedia.org/?curid=4601631#cite_note-:3-6)。

1985年より大学の試合を担当するようになり、3つのボウルゲームの審判を務めた[[3]](https://ja.wikipedia.org/?curid=4601631#cite_note-:2-3)[[6]](https://ja.wikipedia.org/?curid=4601631#cite_note-:3-6)。

1990年にサイドジャッジとしてNFLに採用された。

1995年のNFLのシーズン開始時にレフェリーに昇格したが[[6]](https://ja.wikipedia.org/?curid=4601631#cite_note-:3-6)、これはアフリカ系アメリカ人としてジョニー・グリアー（Johnny Grier）に次いでNFL史上2人目であった[[2]](https://ja.wikipedia.org/?curid=4601631#cite_note-:1-2)。

2005年10月3日、マイクとドン・キャリーは、[カロライナ・パンサーズ](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E3%82%AB%E3%83%AD%E3%83%A9%E3%82%A4%E3%83%8A%E3%83%BB%E3%83%91%E3%83%B3%E3%82%B5%E3%83%BC%E3%82%BA "カロライナ・パンサーズ")と[グリーンベイ・パッカーズ](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E3%82%B0%E3%83%AA%E3%83%BC%E3%83%B3%E3%83%99%E3%82%A4%E3%83%BB%E3%83%91%E3%83%83%E3%82%AB%E3%83%BC%E3%82%BA "グリーンベイ・パッカーズ")の試合で同じ審判団に割り当てられ、NFLの試合でともに審判をする最初の兄弟となった[[7]](https://ja.wikipedia.org/?curid=4601631#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://ja.wikipedia.org/?curid=4601631#cite_note-8)。

2005年12月、[デトロイト・ライオンズ](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E3%83%87%E3%83%88%E3%83%AD%E3%82%A4%E3%83%88%E3%83%BB%E3%83%A9%E3%82%A4%E3%82%AA%E3%83%B3%E3%82%BA "デトロイト・ライオンズ")とグリーンベイ・パッカーズのオーバータイム開始時、キャリーは[コイントス](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E3%82%B3%E3%82%A4%E3%83%B3%E3%83%88%E3%82%B9 "コイントス")に使うコインを見つけられなかった。というのも、試合のキックオフの際に、パッカーズの名誉キャプテンを務めていた子供にコインを渡していたからであった。フィールドジャッジがキャリーに1ペニーを渡した[[9]](https://ja.wikipedia.org/?curid=4601631#cite_note-9)。

2005年シーズンのプレーオフ、[タンパベイ・バッカニアーズ](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E3%82%BF%E3%83%B3%E3%83%91%E3%83%99%E3%82%A4%E3%83%BB%E3%83%90%E3%83%83%E3%82%AB%E3%83%8B%E3%82%A2%E3%83%BC%E3%82%BA "タンパベイ・バッカニアーズ")対[ワシントン・レッドスキンズ](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E3%83%AF%E3%82%B7%E3%83%B3%E3%83%88%E3%83%B3%E3%83%BB%E3%83%AC%E3%83%83%E3%83%89%E3%82%B9%E3%82%AD%E3%83%B3%E3%82%BA "ワシントン・レッドスキンズ")戦で、キャリーがレフェリーを務めた。この試合中、レッドスキンズの[ショーン・テイラー](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E3%82%B7%E3%83%A7%E3%83%BC%E3%83%B3%E3%83%BB%E3%83%86%E3%82%A4%E3%83%A9%E3%83%BC "ショーン・テイラー")がバッカニアーズのランニングバックであるマイケル・ピットマンの顔面に唾を吐き、これに対しピットマンはテイラーのヘルメットに平手打ちで報復した[[10]](https://ja.wikipedia.org/?curid=4601631#cite_note-:4-10)。キャリーは、直ちにテイラーを試合から退場させた一方、ピットマンの報復については審判団で協議の上ペナルティを課さないことを決定した[[10]](https://ja.wikipedia.org/?curid=4601631#cite_note-:4-10)。NFL審判部副部長のマイク・ペレイラは、ピットマンにもペナルティを課して両者のペナルティを相殺するのは「適切ではなかっただろう」としてキャリーの対応を認め、「誰かの顔に唾を吐いた選手を退場させなかった審判がいたら、私は失望しただろう」と付け加えた[[11]](https://ja.wikipedia.org/?curid=4601631#cite_note-11)。

[![Image 3: [Mike Carey]](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ac/Mike_Carey.jpg/250px-Mike_Carey.jpg)](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E3%83%95%E3%82%A1%E3%82%A4%E3%83%AB:Mike_Carey.jpg)

2006年のキャリー

2013年シーズンを最後に、キャリーは審判を引退した。

2014年から2シーズンにわたり、[CBSスポーツ](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS%E3%82%B9%E3%83%9D%E3%83%BC%E3%83%84 "CBSスポーツ")のNFL放送に初の審判アナリストとして出演した。

2014年8月のインタビューで、チーム名が蔑称であると感じられることを理由に、ワシントン・レッドスキンズが登場する試合に自分を配置しないようNFLに要請していたことが明らかになった[[12]](https://ja.wikipedia.org/?curid=4601631#cite_note-:5-12)。実際、キャリーは2006年シーズンの開幕週以来、レッドスキンズがかかわるプレシーズンやレギュラーシーズンのゲームを担当していない。

2022年、NFL審判員協会（NFL Referees Association）の名誉賞を受賞した[[13]](https://ja.wikipedia.org/?curid=4601631#cite_note-13)。

2007年シーズンの優勝決定戦、[第42回スーパーボウル](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E7%AC%AC42%E5%9B%9E%E3%82%B9%E3%83%BC%E3%83%91%E3%83%BC%E3%83%9C%E3%82%A6%E3%83%AB "第42回スーパーボウル")において、キャリーはアフリカ系アメリカ人としてNFL史上初めてスーパーボウルでのレフェリーを務めた[[1]](https://ja.wikipedia.org/?curid=4601631#cite_note-:0-1)[[2]](https://ja.wikipedia.org/?curid=4601631#cite_note-:1-2)。

試合では、キャリーの判断が重要なプレーの要因となった。第4クォーター残り1分15秒、サードダウンで、[ニューヨーク・ジャイアンツ](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E3%83%8B%E3%83%A5%E3%83%BC%E3%83%A8%E3%83%BC%E3%82%AF%E3%83%BB%E3%82%B8%E3%83%A3%E3%82%A4%E3%82%A2%E3%83%B3%E3%83%84 "ニューヨーク・ジャイアンツ")の[クォーターバック](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E3%82%AF%E3%82%A9%E3%83%BC%E3%82%BF%E3%83%BC%E3%83%90%E3%83%83%E3%82%AF "クォーターバック")[イーライ・マニング](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E3%82%A4%E3%83%BC%E3%83%A9%E3%82%A4%E3%83%BB%E3%83%9E%E3%83%8B%E3%83%B3%E3%82%B0 "イーライ・マニング")はショットガンからスナップを受けパスを投じようとした。[ニューイングランド・ペイトリオッツ](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E3%83%8B%E3%83%A5%E3%83%BC%E3%82%A4%E3%83%B3%E3%82%B0%E3%83%A9%E3%83%B3%E3%83%89%E3%83%BB%E3%83%9A%E3%82%A4%E3%83%88%E3%83%AA%E3%82%AA%E3%83%83%E3%83%84 "ニューイングランド・ペイトリオッツ")のディフェンダー3人がマニングをタックルしようと掴みかかった。マニングは2人のディフェンダーから逃れると、[ワイドレシーバー](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E3%83%AF%E3%82%A4%E3%83%89%E3%83%AC%E3%82%B7%E3%83%BC%E3%83%90%E3%83%BC_(%E3%82%A2%E3%83%A1%E3%83%AA%E3%82%AB%E3%83%B3%E3%83%95%E3%83%83%E3%83%88%E3%83%9C%E3%83%BC%E3%83%AB) "ワイドレシーバー (アメリカンフットボール)")のデビッド・タイリーに32ヤードのパスを成功させた。タイリーは手とヘルメットを使い地面ぎりぎりでボールをキャッチした。このアクロバティックなプレーは「[ヘルメットキャッチ](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E3%83%98%E3%83%AB%E3%83%A1%E3%83%83%E3%83%88%E3%82%AD%E3%83%A3%E3%83%83%E3%83%81 "ヘルメットキャッチ")」として現在も語り継がれている[[14]](https://ja.wikipedia.org/?curid=4601631#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://ja.wikipedia.org/?curid=4601631#cite_note-15)。ところでNFLのルールでは、審判は選手がディフェンスの「把握と支配下にある」ときは、審判はプレーを止めなければならない。キャリーは、マニングの前進する勢いが止まらなかったため、「把握と制御」が達成されなかったと判断した[[16]](https://ja.wikipedia.org/?curid=4601631#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://ja.wikipedia.org/?curid=4601631#cite_note-:7-17)。このプレーについてキャリーは「マニングがサックされそうだと思った。あれだけの後ろに体重をかけられたクォーターバックが、2、3人の選手に掴まれて引きずられながらも逃げ切ることはめったにない。マニングは頭がまっすぐ前を向いており、必死で逃れようとしていた。そして突然、彼はスピンして、私に向かってきた」と語った[[17]](https://ja.wikipedia.org/?curid=4601631#cite_note-:7-17)。実際マニングはキャリーの目の前数ヤードを走り過ぎるや否や、ダウンフィールドに向き直りパスを成功させたのであった。

1978年1月、キャリーはダウンヒルスキーに関心が向いていた。トラクションを高めるために地面に敷き詰められた砂利が気になり、自宅でゴムのフロアマットを切り、ワイヤーとリベットで不格好なソールプロテクターを制作した。サンタクララ大学の教授の手助けもあり、ポリウレタン製の量産可能なモデルへ改良した[[18]](https://ja.wikipedia.org/?curid=4601631#cite_note-:6-18)。

1979年にキャリーと新妻ウェンディは、ウィンターマウンテンという会社を設立し、「キャットトラック」に代表されるスキー用アクセサリーの販売を開始した[[18]](https://ja.wikipedia.org/?curid=4601631#cite_note-:6-18)。

1984年には寒冷地でのスキー用[ネオプレン](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E3%83%8D%E3%82%AA%E3%83%97%E3%83%AC%E3%83%B3 "ネオプレン")製フェイスマスクで特許を取得していたジョー・エドワーズと手を組みセイラス社を設立した[[19]](https://ja.wikipedia.org/?curid=4601631#cite_note-19)。キャリーはネオプレンの肌触りを良くするために合成繊維のフリースをラミネートすることを考案した[[18]](https://ja.wikipedia.org/?curid=4601631#cite_note-:6-18)。同製品は人気商品となり、セイラス社を一躍有名にした[[18]](https://ja.wikipedia.org/?curid=4601631#cite_note-:6-18)。

Picked apart by another elite quarterback and a far-from-elite performance by the officiating crew, the [Packers](https://bleacherreport.com/green-bay-packers) fell in excruciating fashion, 51-45 in overtime.

Continuing an unsettling string of stunningly poor performances against great quarterbacks, [Kurt Warner](https://bleacherreport.com/kurt-warner) dissected the Packers' vaunted pass defense just as [Ben Roethlisberger](https://bleacherreport.com/ben-roethlisberger) and [Brett Favre](https://bleacherreport.com/brett-favre) had before him.

Factor Warner's cartoonish numbers (29-33 for 379 yards and five touchdowns without a turnover) into the performances turned in by Big Ben and Favre and the Packer secondary has been astonishingly inept against the only great quarterbacks they faced in 2009.

Here are the raw stats over those four games: 99 completions in 138 attempts (71.7 percent completion rate) for 1,397 yards, with 15 touchdowns and zero interceptions for an average passer rating of just under 135.

Two words: Holy #%*!

After another matador performance, you can throw out all of the accolades and positive attention the defense has gotten this season.

Against great passing attacks the Packers just didn't get the job done.

The Cardinals and their bunch formations had their way with the Packers all day, with receivers coming open across the middle from the opening kick.

And while losing safety Atari Bigby was a blow to an already injury-depleted secondary was undoubtedly a factor, facts are facts.

Those performances are flat-out unacceptable for a playoff team to surrender, and it goes without saying that the Packers will never reach the next level giving up those kinds of numbers to playoff-caliber quarterbacks.

Just imagine for a moment the kind of numbers [Drew Brees](https://bleacherreport.com/drew-brees) would have put up on that D next week. Yikes.

But while allowing a quarterback to throw for more touchdown passes than incompletions is generally a recipe for disaster, the prolific Packers offense, led by [Aaron Rodgers](https://bleacherreport.com/aaron-rodgers) in a masterful playoff debut, nearly brought Green Bay back from the dead.

Rallying back from a nightmarish start, Rodgers established a Packers playoff record with 422 yards passing and accounted for five total touchdowns as he desperately attempted to keep pace with Warner and the Cards.

Recovering from deficits of 17-0 and 31-10, Rodgers and his receivers went up and down the field on the Cardinals all day, picking on backup cornerback Michael Adams in one-on-ones whenever possible.

Unfortunately, the officials didn't pick on the Cardinals nearly enough as they missed a number of calls that ultimately crippled the Packers comeback efforts.

On what turned out to the be final play of the game, the aforementioned Adams blitzed Rodgers and got a handful of facemask while forcing the decisive fumble that Cards' linebacker Karlos Dansby housed for the winning score.

Here is a good link to a [shot](http://www.totalpackers.com/2010/01/11/the-season-ending-facemask/ "shot") of the missed facemask.

But that wasn't the only highly questionable miss.

Referees allowed the Cardinals Larry Fitzgerald to club Charles Woodson aside on his 11-yard touchdown pass in the third quarter, while also missing a highly visible holding call on Cullen Jenkins on the same play.

Jenkins was tackled into Kurt Warner on the play and not only was the hold not called, Jenkins was flagged for roughing the passer on the play.

Even the robotic Troy Aikman found that play dubious on both levels.

Throw in a helmet-to-helmet hit on Rodgers earlier in the contest that went unflagged, and you have several missed calls on absolutely critical plays in the game.

Larry Fitzgerald is tough enough to stop without any help. Allow him to assault the corners covering him downfield and you might as well just put the points on the scoreboard.

While it's tough to pin a loss on the referees when a team gives up 51 points, several key missed calls along with the huge early deficit proved to be too much for these Packers to overcome.

Though an extremely tough loss for Packer fans to take, the heartbreaking defeat was ultimately symbolic of Green Bay's season as a whole.

A team brimming with talent alternately displaying its firepower along with its maddening flaws. A tease of potential and inconsistency.

A team I wouldn't want to deal with next season.

2009-10 NFL playoffs
--------------------

The**National Football League playoffs**for the**2009 season**began on January 9, 2010. The postseason tournament concluded with the New Orleans Saints defeating the Indianapolis Colts in Super Bowl XLIV, 31–17, on February 7, at Sun Life Stadium in Miami Gardens, Florida.

The Wild Card round featured three games that were re-matches of Week 17 games.

Further information:National Football League playoffs §Current playoff system

Within each conference, the 4 division winners and the 2 wild card teams(the top two non-division winners with the best overall regular season records) qualified for the playoffs. The 4 division winners are seeded 1 through 4 based on their overall won-lost-tied record, and the wild card teams are seeded 5 and 6. The NFL does not use a fixed bracket playoff system, and there are no restrictions regarding teams from the same division matching up in any round. In the first round, dubbed the _Wild-Card Playoffs_, the 3rd-seeded division winner hosts the 6th seed wild card, and the 4th seed hosts the 5th. The 1 and 2 seeds from each conference then receive a bye in the first round. In the second round, the _Divisional Playoffs_, the number 1 seed hosts the worst surviving seed from the first round (seed 4, 5 or 6), while the number 2 seed will play the other team (seed 3, 4 or 5). The two surviving teams from each conference's divisional playoff games then meet in the respective AFC and NFC Conference Championship games, hosted by the higher seed. Although the Super Bowl, the fourth and final round of the playoffs, is played at a neutral site, the designated home team is based on an annual rotation by conference.

### Saturday, January 9, 2010[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Famericanfootball.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2F2009-10_NFL_playoffs%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D4&uselang=en "Sign in to edit")]

#### AFC: New York Jets 24, Cincinnati Bengals 14[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Famericanfootball.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2F2009-10_NFL_playoffs%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D5&uselang=en "Sign in to edit")]

**Game summary**

|  | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | Total |

| **Jets** | 0 | 14 | 7 | 3 | **24** |

_at Paul Brown Stadium,Cincinnati_

*   **Game time**: 4:30 p.m.EST
*   **Game weather**: 21°F (−6°C), cloudy
*   **Game attendance**: 63,686
*   **Referee**:Bill Leavy(127)
*   **TV announcers(NBC)**:**Tom Hammond**(play-by-play),Joe Theismann and Joe Gibbs(color commentators), and**[Mike Mayock](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/Mike_Mayock "Mike Mayock")**(sideline reporter)

Rookie quarterback Mark Sanchez completed 12 of 15 passes for 181 yards and a touchdown while rookie running back Shonn Greene rushed for 135 yards as New York followed up their 37–0 win over the Bengals in the last week of the regular season with a 24–14 victory.

Bengals rookie Bernard Scott started off the game with a 56-yard kickoff return to the Jets 36-yard line. But two plays later, receiver Laveranues Coles lost a fumble while being tackled by Bryan Thomas. New York was forced to punt on their ensuing drive, and Rico Murray gave the Bengals good field position with a 23-yard return to the New York 45. This time Cincinnati was able to take advantage of their scoring opportunity, driving 45 yards in seven plays and finishing it with Carson Palmer's 11-yard touchdown pass to Coles.

But in the second quarter, the Jets began to take control of the game. First an 11-yard punt return by Jerricho Cotchery to the Bengals 47-yard line set up a touchdown on a 39-yard burst from Greene. Then New York defensive back Darrelle Revis intercepted a pass from Palmer and returned it 21 yards to the Jets 43-yard line. Two plays later, Sanchez converted a 3rd down and 12 with a 14-yard completion to Cotchery, and then followed it up with a 41-yard scoring strike to tight end Dustin Keller.

On their first drive of the second half, Cincinnati drove from their own 12 to the Jets 17-yard line, featuring a 27-yard run by Cedric Benson. But they failed to score as Palmer's pass on third down was incomplete and Shayne Graham missed a 35-yard field goal attempt. Following the missed field goal, New York drove 75 yards in eight plays, with Sanchez completing an 18-yard pass to Cotchery and a 16-yarder to Braylon Edwards before Thomas Jones finished the drive with a 9-yard touchdown run, increasing their lead to 21–7.

Early in the fourth quarter, Benson took off for a 47-yard touchdown run to make it 21–14. But the Jets responded on their ensuing drive, with Sanchez's 43-yard completion to Keller setting up a 20-yard field goal by Jay Feely to put them back up by a two score margin. The Bengals managed one last attempt to get back in the game with a drive to the New York 11-yard line. But Graham missed another field goal, this one from 28 yards, with 3:43 left in regulation.

Benson finished the game with a franchise record 169 rushing yards. The loss for the Bengals gave them their 19th consecutive season without a playoff win, the longest streak among all 32 NFL teams. Sanchez became only the fourth rookie quarterback to win his first playoff game, following Shaun King,Ben Roethlisberger, and Joe Flacco.

Playing in front of a crowd of 92,951, the largest ever to attend an NFL post-season game other than the Super Bowl, Dallas racked up 426 yards and forced four turnovers en route to their first playoff win since 1996. Cowboys quarterback Tony Romo threw for 244 yards and 2 touchdowns, while running back Felix Jones rushed for 148 yards, including a 73-yard touchdown romp in the second half to put the game away.

After a scoreless first quarter, a 40-yard pass interference penalty on Eagles defensive back Sheldon Brown in the end zone set up Romo's 1-yard touchdown pass to tight end John Phillips. Philadelphia quickly responded with a 76-yard touchdown pass from Michael Vick to Jeremy Maclin on the second play on their ensuing drive. But the Cowboys struck back with an 85-yard scoring drive, featuring 18-yard receptions by Jason Witten and Patrick Crayton, along with a key replay challenge that overturned an Eagles interception.Tashard Choice capped off the drive with a 1-yard touchdown run to give Dallas a 14–7 lead.

Philadelphia was forced to punt on their next drive, and Crayton returned the punt 31 yards to his own 41-yard line. On the next play, Romo's 36-yard completion to Miles Austin moved the ball to the Eagles 23, eventually leading to a Shaun Suisham field goal to make the score 17–7. Just 33 seconds later, the Cowboys increased their lead to 24–7 with Romo's 6-yard touchdown pass to Austin after linebacker Bobby Carpenter recovered a fumbled handoff from Vick on the Philadelphia 18-yard line. Then with time running out in the half, Cowboys linebacker Bradie James forced and recovered a fumble from fullback Leonard Weaver on the Eagles 42-yard line, setting up Suisham's second field goal to give Dallas a 27–7 halftime lead.

In the second half, Jones' 73-yard touchdown run increased the lead even more. Meanwhile, the Cowboys defense held the Eagles in check the rest of the game, forcing two turnovers on downs, another fumble, and an interception, while only allowing a meaningless touchdown on a 6-yard pass from Donovan McNabb to DeSean Jackson in the fourth quarter, making the final score 34–14.

The Ravens converted three first-quarter turnovers by Patriots quarterback Tom Brady into 17 points on their way to a 24–0 lead New England could not recover from. It was the Patriots' first home loss of the season and their first home playoff loss in more than 30 years. On top of that, it was the Ravens' first ever win against the Patriots after five consecutive losses.

Baltimore stormed to a 7–0 lead on the first play of the game with Ray Rice's 83-yard touchdown run, the second longest run in NFL playoff history. Then, linebacker Terrell Suggs forced and recovered a fumble from Brady on the Patriots 17-yard line, and they scored another touchdown with a 1-yard run by Le'Ron McClain. Following an exchange of punts, cornerback Chris Carr intercepted a pass from Brady and returned it to the New England 25-yard line, setting up a drive ending in Rice's second touchdown on a 1-yard run. Just two plays after the ensuing kickoff, Ravens safety Ed Reed intercepted a deep pass from Brady and returned it 25 yards before lateraling the ball to safety Dawan Landry, who took it another 25 yards to the Patriots 9-yard line. The Ravens could not gain any yards on their ensuing drive, but Billy Cundiff kicked a field goal to make the score 24–0.

New England was forced to punt on their next drive, but Baltimore returner Tom Zbikowski muffed the catch and Kyle Arrington recovered the ball for the Patriots at the Ravens 16-yard line. Five plays later, Brady threw a 6-yard touchdown pass to Julian Edelman. Midway through the second half, Brady threw his third interception of the game, this one to Landry, who returned it 42 yards to the New England 22-yard line to set up another Cundiff field goal. Taking the ball back to the Patriots 47-yard line after Darius Butler's 42-yard kickoff return, New England responded with a 53-yard scoring drive. Brady finished it with his second touchdown pass to Edelman to cut their deficit to 27–14.

Zbikowski returned the ensuing kickoff 30 yards to his own 48-yard line, sparking a 52-yard drive that ended with a 3-yard touchdown run from Willis McGahee, making the score 33–14 after the two-point conversion failed. New England responded with a drive deep into Baltimore territory, but Stephen Gostkowski missed a 44-yard field goal attempt with 7:19 left in the game, ending any chance of a miracle comeback.

Rice rushed for 159 yards and two touchdowns, while McGahee added 62 yards and a score. Neither quarterback had much success, as Brady was held to 154 yards and intercepted three times, while Baltimore's Joe Flacco completed only 4 of 10 passes for 34 yards.

The presentation of the flag and singing of The Star-Spangled Banner before the start of the Packers vs. Cardinals Wild Card Game.

This high scoring shootout set the NFL postseason record for most points (96), touchdowns (13), and first downs (62), while ranking third in total yards (1,024). But in the end, it was a defensive play that made the key difference when Cardinals linebacker Karlos Dansby returned a fumble 17 yards for a touchdown in overtime. This was only the second overtime game in NFL postseason history ever to be won by a defensive touchdown. The first one had been won by the Packers (vs. Seahawks in 2003).

Arizona forced two early turnovers and built up a quick 17–0 lead. First, defensive back Dominique Rodgers-Cromartie's interception of an Aaron Rodgers pass set up a 1-yard touchdown run by Tim Hightower. Then Dansby forced a fumble from Packers receiver Donald Driver that defensive tackle Alan Branch recovered on the Green Bay 22-yard line, leading to Kurt Warner's 15-yard touchdown pass to Early Doucet. After a Green Bay punt, Warner led the Cardinals down the field, hitting Larry Fitzgerald for 14 yards, tight end Ben Patrick for 22, and Steve Breaston for 15 on the way to a 23-yard field goal from Neil Rackers.

Early in the second quarter, Packers cornerback Charles Woodson stripped the ball from Fitzgerald, and linebacker Clay Matthews returned the fumble 28 yards to the Green Bay 48. Aided by three Cardinals penalties, Green Bay drove 52 yards and scored on a 1-yard run from Rodgers. Arizona responded by driving 79 yards and scoring with Warner's second touchdown pass to Doucet. But Rodgers struck back with a pair of completions to tight end Jermichael Finley for gains of 44 and 17 yards on the way to a 20-yard field by Mason Crosby, cutting the score to 24–10 at halftime.

The second half opened up with five touchdowns on five consecutive drives. First, Warner threw his third touchdown pass of the day with a 33-yard strike to Fitzgerald. Rodgers responded with an 18-yard completion to Finley and a 35-yard bomb to Greg Jennings before Jennings finished the drive with a 6-yard touchdown catch. Then Green Bay surprised Arizona with an onside kick, which Brandon Underwood recovered on the Packers 43-yard line. Seven plays later, Rodgers threw a 10-yard touchdown pass to Jordy Nelson, cutting their deficit to 31–24. But a few plays after the ensuing kickoff,Beanie Wells' 42-yard run set up an 11-yard touchdown pass from Warner to Fitzgerald.

Early in the fourth quarter, Rodgers again closed the gap to one score with a 30-yard touchdown pass to James Jones. Then after forcing a punt, Rodgers completed a 38-yard strike to Finley and a 28-yarder to Driver at the Cardinals 1-yard line. Fullback John Kuhn scored a 1-yard touchdown run on the next play to tie the game. But Arizona retook it with their next drive as Warner completed seven passes, the last one a 17-yard touchdown toss to Breaston. Taking the ball back at the 29-yard line with just under five minutes left in regulation, Rodgers hit Jones for 6 yards, scrambled for 13 yards, and then hit Jennings for 22 yards and a first down at the Arizona 25-yard line. A few plays later, he finished the drive with an 11-yard touchdown pass to Spencer Havner, tying the game with less than 2 minutes to go. Arizona responded with a drive to the Green Bay 16-yard line, but Rackers missed a 34-yard field goal as time expired, sending the game into overtime.

Green Bay won the coin toss and got the ball first. But two plays into their drive, Cardinals defensive back Michael Adams sacked Rodgers as he was about to throw. The ball came out of Rodgers' hands, and a desperate Rodgers tried to kick the loose ball out of bounds, but it got away and went into the arms of Dansby, who returned the fumble 17 yards for a touchdown to win the game.

In his first career playoff game, Rodgers set a franchise record with 422 passing yards and four touchdowns. Warner completed 29 of 33 passes for 379 yards and a franchise record five touchdowns. He became the second player in NFL history ever to throw five touchdown passes in two different postseason games, joining Daryle Lamonica(Warner had thrown five touchdown passes in his first NFL playoff game a decade earlier). The Cardinals' 51 points was the most ever allowed by the Packers in their 41 postseason games. Arizona gained 531 total yards, with 156 rushing yards, against a Packers defense that finished the season ranked first in the NFL against the run and second fewest yards allowed overall.
